source.original_title: 07/03/2026 - Michael Mazey x Michael Brideau KFS
source.display_title: 07/03/2026 - Michael Mazey x Michael Brideau KFS — Closed

call.sequence_note: Second call with this prospect. The rep opens 'I'm excited to chat with you again, bro' and refers back to 'I mentioned this yesterday', then recites a goal list gathered previously — 'we talked about a number of different goals, right? Becoming the best man you can be. We want to address some weaknesses in shoulder up the body. We want to create athleticism to help improve ping pong and other sports, confidence, like dating, you know, have an at-home routine.' The frame, baseline and past-attempts work were run on the earlier call, which is not in this batch. This file therefore cannot verify what medical or injury screening took place.

rep.name: Michael Brideau
rep.location: Medellín, Colombia — relocating to Florianópolis, Brazil within five to six days; Canadian, raised in Peace River, Alberta

prospect.name: Michael Mazey
prospect.training_background: Former cross-country runner, self-described as having been 'skin and bones'. Currently active across several sports — competitive table tennis with a dedicated coach, plus volleyball and basketball. Travels frequently and wants a routine he can do at home. Also engaged with a separate dating coach. Found Primal Instinct through his Instagram feed.

signals: Frames the purchase as self-optimisation from an already-functioning base rather than rescue: 'the root is, like, being the best self, which is kind of, like, fundamental to everything, so everything stems from that'

Already a habitual buyer of coaching and treats it as a status-normal behaviour: 'I underestimated the power of coaching for a long time, because I thought there was a cool factor in just, like, being self-taught' and is concurrently paying for dating coaching
Identity-driven language throughout — 'main character' versus 'NPC', 'Michael 2.0', proving people wrong about genetics

Tension with the archetype: price was not frictionless. He asked for a payment plan twice and disclosed a short-term spending constraint — 'I've like spent so much in the last like two, three months that it's like, I honestly probably need to start holding back a little bit' — and was actively checking a credit card limit while paying. A textbook optimizer treats price as a quality signal; this one was managing headroom.
No occupation, income, age or family detail was established anywhere in this call, so the 'already successful' half of the archetype is asserted by manner rather than evidenced

goals.text: Become the best version of himself — named as the root goal that everything else stems from
Address upper body and shoulder weakness
Build athleticism that transfers into table tennis and his other sports
Fix his posture — believes the visual problem is arrangement rather than mass
Have a simple at-home routine that survives frequent travel
Protect his joints and avoid accumulating long-term injuries
Prove wrong the idea that genetics determine outcomes — 'when someone says that you can't do something, it almost gives you a lot of fuel to prove them wrong'
Set an example that pushes back on what Trevor calls modern man syndrome, and eventually pass the knowledge on to others

pains.text: Inconsistent eating and frequent eating out
Poor posture and shoulder positioning he has only recently started working on
Time scarcity from being 'all in on everything' — names time as the single limiting factor on commitment
Has historically avoided coaching out of a belief that being self-taught was better, and thinks that cost him years
Short-term cash pressure after heavy recent spending, and managing available credit — 'I'm thinking about which credit card do you use to stay under the limit'
Finds the people around him unmotivated and says it drags on him — 'if you're around people that don't have a whole lot of passion, it just kind of gives off a bad vibe to you'
Sugar habit he is aware of and rationalises — opened the call drinking a mocha McFrappé he described as a reward habit

objections.raw_quote: Yeah, that's, that's good. I mean, now it's a matter of like, is it possible to have like a payment plan? Because, I mean, I think I could probably do it all at once, but like, it does make it easier to have like space out a bit, if it's possible. Like, I just didn't, that's the one thing I don't want to say, like, I've like spent so much in the last like two, three months that it's like, I honestly probably need to start holding back a little bit.
objections.rep_response: Did not answer the question. Responded with a spending anecdote about himself — 'I've spent almost 150 grand on coaching and mentorship and personal development the last, like, six years' — then, when the prospect asked a second time, said 'Can I shoot it straight with you? Dude, I think if you can do it all right now, I think you should' and justified it with a claim that students who pay in full get the best results. Whether a payment plan exists was never stated either way.

offer.guarantee_mentioned: Disclosed only after the card was charged, in response to the prospect reading the agreement: 'we guarantee that you'll actually increase your, your weight on your key list by eight kilograms, and if you don't, now, you do have to hit the, there's specific metrics, like, you have to hit, like, 90% of the workouts and different things like that, you'll read that in a second, but if you don't, Trevor will actually continue working with you for free until you do. And provided you complete the program in six months, you get $500 credit towards either future coaching, or there's a few other things as well.'

evidence: Paid in full on the call by Discover card, keyed by the rep into the payment processor and confirmed live: 'it went through perfect, man. So we're all good to rock on that.'
Agreement signed on the call — 'can you pop that open and just do a quick autograph on it for me?' … 'Yeah, so you did, you did autograph it, though. Like, you submitted it, correct?' … 'Yeah.'
Onboarding call with Trevor booked, initially Monday 5:45 pm Eastern, then rescheduled live to Tuesday 5:15 pm Eastern when a conflict surfaced.
Skool community sign-up and the onboarding form were both instructed and the form was texted over during the call.

Counter-evidence on process quality rather than on the close itself: the prospect asked for a payment plan twice and was steered to pay in full while checking whether he was under his credit card limit, and he signed the agreement after saying 'I'll just skim in real quick'.
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor on Tuesday at 5:15 pm Eastern. Prospect to sign up for the Skool community and complete the onboarding form beforehand. Rep relocating to Brazil within the week and handing the relationship to Trevor — 'Probably mainly be Trevor, dude.'

notable.note: Cleanest P11 in the batch and the weakest front half. The full card number, expiry and security code were spoken aloud and are captured verbatim in this stored transcript — a systemic exposure, not a one-off, since the rep's stated method is 'I'll just grab the number and punch it in here in our payment processor.' Separately, the prospect twice asked whether a payment plan was available, disclosed that he had overspent recently and was checking his credit limit mid-purchase, and never received an answer; he was talked into paying $6,000 in full instead. Payment plans demonstrably exist elsewhere in this corpus. Also worth a manager's attention: the guarantee and its 90%-compliance condition were first explained after the money was taken, and no consequence frame was run at any point on this call — it closed purely on enthusiasm.

quality.notes: Intermittent rather than continuous. The two participants share a first name, which compounds it. Clear inversions include the prospect's turn at 00:05:32 that is actually the rep delivering the customisation pitch, the rep's turn at 00:56 on accountability that runs into the prospect's reply, and the exchange around 00:12:18 to 00:12:48. Roles were resolved from content: the rep is whoever delivers the pillars, quotes $6,000 and takes the card. The opening minute is an unpunctuated run-on block attributed to the prospect that actually contains both voices.
